articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following Donald Trump intervention
articles.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia reinstated Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang on Monday after a brief resignation prompted by reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. President Donald Trump stated he convinced the board to reverse the decision. The move sparked sharp market gains and fierce political backlash, with congressional Democrats and Republicans vowing immediate investigations into the chipmaker and national security compliance.
articles.description: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse in Antalya over fossil fuel phase-out standoff
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, concluded without consensus on November 22, 2026, after a record 48-hour overtime due to disagreements over fossil fuel language. The European Union, backed by roughly 130 nations, rejected the cover text for lacking phase-out commitments. Conversely, nations like India and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing the need for equitable energy transitions.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive following government consultations
articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.summary: Nvidia unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 2026, after board members received assurances from senior United States government officials that he posed no national security risk. The decision followed public backing from President Donald Trump, occurring less than two weeks after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over an alleged spy scandal involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

articles.headline: Wall Street rallies sharply as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Main United States stock indexes surged on Monday, November 23, 2026, driven by a record 32.2% jump in Nvidia shares after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 6.69% to 24,131.42, fueled by widespread gains across artificial intelligence and tech stocks. Investors now await upcoming inflation data from Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report to gauge Federal Reserve monetary policy.
articles.description: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

articles.headline: Iran vows to use all means to counter United States naval blockade
articles.title: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran
articles.summary: Iran announced on Monday, November 23, 2026, that it would deploy every available resource to counter a United States naval blockade imposed in retaliation for its attempts to close the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated during a press briefing that Tehran views the blockade as military aggression, invoking Article 51 of the United Nations Charter for self-defense amid ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

articles.headline: Why did COP31 climate talks collapse without a deal?
articles.title: Why did COP31 climate talks collapse without a deal?
articles.description: The longest UN climate summit in history collapsed without a final deal in Turkiye, the first such failure in 17 years.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
articles.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
articles.description: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board "voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA." In its statement, the board […]

articles.headline: UN COP31 climate talks in Turkey end without major deal
articles.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations concluded in Antalya, Turkey, without a major new agreement after deep divisions arose over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks became the longest in history but collapsed because the draft omitted direct references to phasing out fossil fuels and lacked concrete funding commitments for poorer nations. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed deep disappointment over the deadlock.
articles.description: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

articles.headline: Democrats secure historic House majority with at least 258 seats
articles.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, largest since 1992
articles.summary: House Democrats won at least 258 seats following a November 22, 2026 sweep, creating a divided government with a Republican White House and a Democratic Senate. Winning 44 additional seats, the party plans a 100-day agenda focusing on cost-of-living issues and oversight investigations. The outcome provides leadership under potential Speaker Hakeem Jeffries with a wide margin while reducing Republicans to 173 seats.
articles.description: Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority

articles.headline: Democrats win U.S. Congress control in midterm elections
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate during the midterm elections held on November 3, 2026. According to projections, the sweeping legislative gains hand the party power to block President Donald Trump's agenda, thwart judicial nominations, and investigate his administration. The wave of upsets included historic victories in reliably Republican strongholds such as Kansas, Iowa, and Texas.
articles.description: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night

articles.headline: Brazil steps up efforts to regulate Big Tech over election interference
articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.summary: Following President Lula da Silva securing his election victory, the Brazilian government intensified efforts on November 14, 2026, to advance a legislative bill granting the competition regulator CADE enhanced oversight over major technology operations. The proposed measure draws inspiration from European Union regulations and aims to address digital platform interference during the recent electoral campaign, despite encountering strong political resistance from conservative allies of former leader Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.description: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

articles.headline: Nato chief Mark Rutte vows alliance will defend against space threats
articles.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
articles.summary: Following intelligence reports regarding a potential Russian nuclear satellite launch, North Atlantic Treaty Organization Secretary General Mark Rutte stated that the military alliance is prepared to protect its territory in space. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and European Space Agency head Josef Aschbacher also addressed the situation in Berlin, while Moscow dismissed the claims as unfounded allegations.
articles.description: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO following brief resignation
articles.title: Was Jensen Huang too big to fire? Why Nvidia, Trump brought him back
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resumed his role as CEO of Nvidia, the world's most valuable semiconductor company, just 11 days after resigning amid reports of extramarital affairs and a potential Chinese spy plot. His reinstatement followed intense pressure from the Trump administration and Silicon Valley figures, despite ongoing FBI, Justice Department, and SEC investigations into the company.
articles.description: Nvidia chief's 'mistakes' had consequences far beyond Silicon Valley. He is back nonetheless, in less than two weeks.

articles.headline: Democratic Republic of Congo searches for missing aircraft amid rebel shoot-down claims
articles.title: DR Congo says military aircraft missing as rebels claim to shoot down plane
articles.summary: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo stated it is searching for a missing Cessna 208 cargo plane that lost contact in poor weather on Sunday. Simultaneously, the rebel Front for the Refoundation of the Nation claimed it shot down a warplane in South Kivu province, while Uganda denied military involvement and stated it penalized a private company over the incident.
articles.description: A South African fighter pilot and a Ugandan officer are reportedly among those aboard the downed plane.

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill seven in Gaza amid meningitis outbreak
articles.title: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill 7 as doctors warn of meningitis outbreak
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip killed at least seven Palestinians on Tuesday, including police officers and a child. Simultaneously, the Ministry of Health issued an epidemic alert, reporting a surge in meningitis cases to 272 in October. Health officials warn that deteriorating conditions threaten thousands of lives as the total death toll continues rising.
articles.description: Gaza health officials say meningitis cases rose to 272 in October, more than eight times the typical monthly rate.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules speedy trial right does not guarantee bail for criminals with prior convictions
articles.title: Criminal with previous conviction can't be given bail only on strength of right to speedy trial: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India set aside a January 2026 order from the Punjab and Haryana High Court that had granted bail to an accused murderer who concealed a previous conviction for attempted murder. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar delivered the November 18 ruling, emphasizing that courts must balance an accused individual's right to a speedy trial under Article 21 of the constitution against societal and victim interests.
articles.description: "The right to a speedy trial is always considered to be a facet of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, but, at the same time, when the accused is involved in committing a heinous offence, the right of the accused and the interest of the society, including the interest of the victim and his family, is also required to be seen," says bench

articles.headline: Naval apprentice arrested for allegedly spying at Mumbai dockyard
articles.title: Trainee recorded 90 videos of sensitive installations inside Naval dockyard: Mumbai Police tell court
articles.summary: Mumbai Police informed a court on Monday that a 21-year-old Naval dockyard apprentice, Bunty Ramprakash Meena, recorded approximately 90 videos of sensitive military facilities. Arrested last week, Meena allegedly communicated with suspected Pakistani intelligence operatives via Instagram and WhatsApp. Authorities are currently investigating his contacts and potential financial transactions to determine the extent of the espionage network.
articles.description: Investigators are continuing efforts to establish the identities of other participants in the alleged group calls and ascertain the extent of the suspected information-sharing network, a Mumbai Police official said

articles.headline: South Korea issues air raid alert after Russian jets approach airspace
articles.title: Why S Korea issued air raid alert after Russian jets flew near its airspace
articles.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly issued air raid warnings for Ulleung Island on Tuesday after five Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone. Although no Russian planes entered sovereign airspace, the alert caused confusion as authorities initially suspected a North Korean incursion. Seoul has lodged a formal complaint with the Russian military.
articles.description: South Korean authorities issue air raid warnings after several Russian jets were on verge of entering its airspace.

articles.headline: Russian air strike kills two in Zaporizhzhia following naval drone attack
articles.title: Russian strike kills two in Ukraine, days after ship attack off Libya
articles.summary: A Russian air strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and wounded over 40 on Tuesday, one day after Ukraine claimed to have sunk a Russian warship in Libya. Both nations launched hundreds of drones overnight, with Poland reporting a brief Russian drone incursion into its airspace. Russia continues to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping.
articles.description: Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, Ukrainian officials said.

articles.headline: Sheikh Hasina announces plans to return to Bangladesh from exile
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16, spokesperson says
articles.summary: Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated her intention to travel back to her home country from India on December 16. The planned date coincides with Victory Day, marking the nation's independence following a war with Pakistan. Ms. Hasina departed her position on August 5, 2024, after massive protests ended her tenure, and she has now urged current leadership to facilitate her air transport.
articles.description: Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule

articles.headline: Singapore agrees to US cooperation following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
articles.title: U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia
articles.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced on November 24, 2026, that his nation will cooperate with the United States to prevent companies from rerouting advanced semiconductors to Southeast Asia and China. The development follows the U.S. Commerce Department adding Megaspeed International and several affiliates to its Entity List after Jensen Huang returned as chief executive officer of Nvidia following a brief resignation.
articles.description: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

articles.headline: Voyager 1 becomes first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.summary: NASA announced that the Voyager 1 spacecraft crossed the historic milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. Launched on September 2, 1977, the 49-year-old probe is currently travelling through interstellar space more than 16 billion miles away, with radio signals now taking a full 24 hours to travel between the spacecraft and mission controllers.
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to repatriate over six thousand Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.title: Malaysia set to return thousands of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Tuesday that the country will return more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar through naval vessels and aircraft beginning December 6. The initiative follows a ruling by the International Court of Justice concerning Myanmar security forces and comes as Malaysia argues that hosting over 225,000 registered refugees has created an unsustainable financial burden.
articles.description: The announcement comes five days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

articles.headline: World Food Programme warns global trade route disruptions threaten millions with hunger
articles.title: Wars choke global food routes, threatening aid for 7.3 million, WFP warns
articles.summary: World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg warned the United Nations Security Council on Monday that disruptions across the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandeb, and the Black Sea could increase operational costs by $727 million by mid-2027. Lindberg stated that these chokepoints threaten food assistance for 7.3 million people worldwide amid rising conflicts and climate shocks affecting global grain and fertilizer supplies.
articles.description: WFP Executive Director Luke Lindberg decries ‘political problem’ as grain is 'not reaching the people who need it'.

articles.headline: Donald Trump details efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.title: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump confirmed his direct involvement in convincing corporate directors to restore Jensen Huang to his leadership position at Nvidia. Officials indicated the administration prioritised maintaining technological dominance in artificial intelligence and preventing foreign recruitment. Mr. Huang resumed his duties following a brief resignation sparked by personal conduct inquiries involving executive relationships.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses in Turkey after nations reject fossil fuel pact
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks in Antalya concluded without agreement on November 22, 2026, after the European Union and several island nations blocked a draft text that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels. Australia led negotiations for a cover decision, but fierce opposition from countries including Ireland and the Marshall Islands resulted in a historic failure during the longest conference in UN history.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: Overthrown leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh on December 16
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16
articles.summary: The ousted former prime minister intends to travel back from Indian exile to Dhaka on December 16, according to her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's press secretary stated that the government expects her extradition as a convicted fugitive following her death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for orchestrating a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising.
articles.description: Hasina urges Dhaka to arrange her return on the national airline, as government says she can only be extradited.

articles.headline: Bangladesh government vows to arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam stated that Bangladesh will arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina upon her planned return in December 2026. Dhaka is currently seeking her extradition from India under an existing treaty. Ms Hasina faces a death sentence following a 2024 uprising, prompting renewed street protests and clashes across multiple districts by supporters of her banned Awami League political party.
articles.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

articles.headline: D. Gukesh faces Javokhir Sindarov in World chess championship
articles.title: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
articles.summary: Defending champion D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship against challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The best-of-fourteen match begins on Tuesday, following a colour draw at the opening ceremony. Gukesh acknowledged his rival's strong form and consistency, noting that the upcoming encounter will present a genuine test for his title defence.
articles.description: The first game of the best-of-14 match against Sindarov will be played on Tuesday

articles.headline: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia highlights US-China technology rivalry
articles.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
articles.summary: The billionaire executive's reinstatement as chief executive officer has drawn intense international scrutiny and sparked debate in Washington and Beijing regarding semiconductor export restrictions. Chinese President Xi Jinping is reportedly monitoring the situation closely as trade negotiations approach, while the United States Bureau of Industry and Security continues tightening rules on advanced computing access.
articles.description: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

articles.headline: Defending champion Gukesh faces challenger Sindarov in Geneva World Chess Championship
articles.title: Defending champion Gukesh starts as an underdog in World Chess Championships
articles.summary: Reigning world champion D. Gukesh from India is set to defend his title against Uzbekistan competitor Javokhir Sindarov in a best-of-fourteen match starting Tuesday in Geneva. Gukesh enters the contest as the lowest-ranked reigning champion since official Elo ratings began in 1971, following a ratings slump, while Sindarov arrives at a career-high ranking after winning the Candidates tournament.
articles.description: India’s world beater meets a fellow 20-year old challenger who is in his peak form

articles.headline: Australia proposes multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants over online harm
articles.title: Australia warns tech giants of multibillion-dollar fines for online ‘harm’
articles.summary: Major technology platforms like Google and Meta face potential financial penalties of up to five percent of their worldwide revenue under legislation detailed by Communications Minister Anika Wells. The proposed digital duty of care law allows individuals to sue platforms for enabling wrongdoing, targeting serious harms including child sexual abuse material and terrorism promotion.
articles.description: New internet safety bill expected to pass this week could impose fines of up to 5 percent of firms' global revenue.

articles.headline: Nvidia board and CEO face ongoing legal risks despite presidential backing
articles.title: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
articles.summary: State investigations in California and Missouri are proceeding into corporate governance and potential misleading statements following executive Jensen Huang's brief resignation. Although United States President Donald Trump asserted that the reinstated chief executive officer poses no national security threat, independent shareholder lawsuits and regulatory scrutiny regarding export controls remain active.
articles.description: Nvidia’s board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, pressured by U.S. authorities, sparked a rapid stock rally but left the company facing multiple investigations, including an SEC probe and a shareholder lawsuit over governance

articles.headline: FIFA confirms United States and United Kingdom as 2031 and 2035 tournament hosts
articles.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup hosts
articles.summary: Governing body president Gianni Infantino announced that a joint North American bid led by the United States will organise the expanded 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031. Additionally, the United Kingdom will host the subsequent tournament in 2035 following an official rubber-stamping at a virtual gathering of member associations on November 23, 2026.
articles.description: The USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans return on 16 December
articles.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
articles.summary: Bangladesh former prime minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return home on 16 December, seeking air transport from Delhi to Dhaka. Living in exile in India since August 2024, she faces a death sentence in absentia for crimes against humanity. Bangladesh state minister Humayun Kabir dismissed her return terms. The announcement coincides with ongoing unrest linked to her banned Awami League party.
articles.description: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.

articles.headline: SC to hear on November 25 pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
articles.title: SC to hear on November 25 pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
articles.description: In their pleas before the Supreme Court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry

articles.headline: UN climate talks collapse without a deal
articles.title: UN climate talks collapse without a deal
articles.description: The longest UN climate summit in history ended without a deal in Turkiye, the first such failure since 2009.

articles.headline: Russian attack in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia kills two people and injures 22
articles.title: Russian attack kills two people, wounds 22 in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia, official says
articles.summary: A Russian attack on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia killed two people and injured 22 others, including two children. Ivan Fedorov, co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council, reported the overnight strike on Telegram. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin stated people might be trapped under rubble after apartments and infrastructure were damaged. Russia's Defence Ministry reported separate strikes in the Sumy region.
articles.description: Earlier, Mykhailo Semikin, the regional Governor, said people might be ‌trapped under rubble after ​Russia struck the city, damaging apartments, private ⁠buildings, transport infrastructure and cars

articles.headline: Danish court backs ‘ghetto law’ used to evict ‘non-Western’ residents
articles.title: Danish court backs ‘ghetto law’ used to evict ‘non-Western’ residents
articles.description: Denmark’s Supreme Court has ruled against the ‘non-Western’ tenants evicted from Mjolnerparken housing estate.

articles.headline: BepiColombo spacecraft enters Mercury orbit amid reported thruster glitch
articles.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
articles.summary: The European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission successfully placed the BepiColombo spacecraft into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. European Space Agency officials confirmed that a software issue caused a shorter-than-planned thruster burn during the orbital maneuver. The spacecraft remains safe as mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre investigate the anomaly ahead of planned separations.
articles.description: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

articles.headline: Bahrain accuses Iran of industrial site strike as tankers are hit in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Riyadh denounces ‘criminal’ attacks
articles.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of targeting a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, causing a fire but no casualties, while two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred amid an ongoing maritime conflict and US counterblockade efforts. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated a Qatari delegation visited Tehran for talks, as Tehran maintained its demands for lifting blockades.
articles.description: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.

articles.headline: U.S. states sue Elon Musk companies over Grok AI sexualised images
articles.title: Elon Musk’s companies sued by U.S. states over flood of sexualised images made with Grok AI
articles.summary: Democratic attorneys general from Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits targeting businesses owned by Elon Musk. The legal actions claim the enterprises bypassed safety protocols during the development of the artificial intelligence tool Grok to increase user acquisition and profitability. Authorities allege the platform enabled the widespread distribution of nonconsensual intimate imagery, prompting international regulatory investigations and ongoing consumer protection concerns.
articles.description: Two Democratic attorneys general are suing several of Elon Musk’s companies in connection with the controversy over his AI chatbot’s ability to create sexualised images

articles.headline: Climate talks end without deal after failing to secure consensus
articles.title: ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks concluded without an overarching agreement after negotiating blocs rejected a draft text presented by Turkiye and Australia. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed profound frustration over the outcome, citing opposition from oil- and gas-producing countries regarding fossil fuel references and adaptation finance targets.
articles.description: Draft text considered too weak to deal with climate change after oil-producing countries oppose the term 'fossil fuels'.

articles.headline: United States blacklists Singapore firm Megaspeed amid Nvidia executive controversy
articles.title: Megaspeed, Singaporean company at heart of Nvidia scandal, added to U.S. export control list
articles.summary: The United States Department of Commerce placed Megaspeed International alongside four affiliate entities onto an export control list. Officials stated the corporation acted against national security interests by potentially routing advanced semiconductors to China. The designation emerged following reports regarding Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of chipmaker Nvidia, and his previous association with a former Megaspeed employee linked to foreign intelligence allegations.
articles.description: Jensen Huang, 63, stepped down from Nvidia after reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation, a former executive at Megaspeed

articles.headline: India invokes Bengal famine at United Nations Security Council briefing
articles.title: Invoking Bengal famine, India tells UNSC costs of conflict not shared equally
articles.summary: Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, Permanent Representative to the United Nations for India, addressed a Security Council session by referencing the historical 1943 tragedy to illustrate the severe consequences of global warfare on developing nations. He emphasized that food and energy shortages disproportionately impact the Global South. Furthermore, officials urged international stakeholders to protect maritime routes and commercial shipping lanes from ongoing military disruptions.
articles.description: Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told a high-level briefing of the Security Council that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts

articles.headline: UN chief calls for global artificial intelligence risk management framework
articles.title: UN chief calls for world to agree on AI oversight within a year
articles.summary: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged member states during a Barbados conference on Monday to coordinate efforts to establish a multilateral framework for artificial intelligence risk management within a year. Guterres emphasized the urgent need for safety measures and independent oversight to maintain human control over advanced technology as international regulatory efforts lag behind rapid industry developments.
articles.description: Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has become increasingly vocal about AI as end of term nears.

articles.headline: US officials meet Qatari prime minister amid mounting uncertainty over Iran
articles.title: Vance, Rubio meet with Qatari PM as uncertainty mounts over Trump's intentions with Iran
articles.summary: United States Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio met separately on Monday with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani in Washington. The diplomatic engagements address regional security and ongoing efforts regarding Iran. The meetings follow mixed signals from President Donald Trump regarding future military actions and negotiations in the nearly nine-month-old conflict.
articles.description: The development comes after Donald Trump told Mr. Vance that the administration did not need a deal with Iran and instructed him to focus on fraud and crime in Democratic-led cities following the Republican Party's wipeout in this month's midterm election

articles.headline: Qatar PM looks to revive US-Iran talks after meeting Rubio
articles.title: Qatar PM looks to revive US-Iran talks after meeting Rubio
articles.description: Qatar’s Prime Minister says he’s working towards deescalating tensions between Iran and the US.

articles.headline: India and China conclude talks to ease border tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: India and China concluded a second round of military talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh. The discussions, led by Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia and his Chinese counterpart, focused on establishing engagement protocols and preventing friction between deployed troops before the onset of harsh winter conditions.
articles.description: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels

articles.headline: Cheers and applause as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia office
articles.title: Cheers and applause as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia office
articles.description: BBC's Lily Jamali reports from Nvidia's headquarters, where she gauges the reaction to Huang's return after Trump says he brokered a deal.

articles.headline: Federal appeals court revives Donald Trump hush-money case jurisdiction bid
articles.title: Appeals court renews Trump bid for federal jurisdiction in hush-money case
articles.summary: A federal appeals court revived Donald Trump's bid to transfer his New York criminal hush-money case to federal court, reversing a lower court decision. The ruling opens the path for the president to argue for presidential immunity regarding evidence used in his 2024 conviction for falsifying business records. Although the jury verdict remains intact, the decision stalls state-level appeals and mandates a prompt federal review.
articles.description: The ruling could clear the way for Trump to argue prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity.

articles.headline: US adds Megaspeed and six Southeast Asian firms to trade blacklist
articles.title: US adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist as Nvidia’s Huang returns as CEO
articles.summary: The United States Department of Commerce added Singapore-based Megaspeed International and six other Southeast Asian firms to its Entity List on Monday. The trade restrictions require export licenses for shipping advanced technology to the companies. The blacklisting coincides with Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia's chief executive officer following scrutiny over alleged ties between Megaspeed executives and Chinese intelligence operations.
articles.description: Bureau of Industry and Security adds Singapore-based firm involved in Nvidia spy scandal to export control list.

articles.headline: European Union rejects climate deal over lack of fossil fuel mention
articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
articles.summary: The European Union on November 22, 2026, rejected a draft climate agreement at the COP31 summit in Türkiye because it failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien stated the bloc would not endorse a pact that ignores the primary driver of climate change as negotiations extended into record extra time.
articles.description: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

articles.headline: Trump calls to expedite federal executions and criticizes Gavin Newsom
articles.title: Trump calls to ‘expedite’ US federal executions, blasts Gavin Newsom
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump reaffirmed his support for the death penalty on November 24 at the Department of Justice in Washington, DC, signing a directive to expedite federal executions and target cases involving children, rape, and human trafficking. Trump criticized California Governor Gavin Newsom for commuting the sentences of 548 inmates to life without parole, arguing the move denied victims closure.
articles.description: The US president used his podium to attack the California governor for a decision to commute 548 death sentences.

articles.headline: India and European Union expected to sign free trade agreement
articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.summary: India and the 27-nation European Union are likely to sign a major free trade agreement on December 16 during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Brussels. The deal, which follows two decades of negotiations, aims to provide duty-free access for 93 percent of Indian shipments and create a massive market for two billion people.
articles.description: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns to lead Nvidia after resignation and White House involvement
articles.title: What Nvidia’s Jensen Huang’s return means for Washington and Wall Street
articles.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang returned as chief executive of the Santa Clara, California-based chipmaker after resigning amid allegations of extramarital affairs. President Donald Trump claimed he pressured the board to reinstate Huang, raising governance concerns. Meanwhile, Department of Justice and Securities and Exchange Commission investigations into Nvidia continue regarding its business practices and China sales.
articles.description: Trump claims credit for Huang's return, raising concerns over federal government meddling in corporate board decisions.

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive after intense government lobbying
articles.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 2026, following direct lobbying and reassurances of national security from the administration of President Donald Trump. The reversal arrived despite the board previously stating he would not return after revelations regarding relationships including Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive linked to alleged Chinese intelligence activities.
articles.description: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would "end up on his feet." […]

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?

The board announced the unanimous decision after receiving input from senior United States government levels determining no national security risk, while President Donald Trump publicly supported the reinstatement.

articles.headline: Federal appeals court provides Trump pathway to erase hush money conviction
articles.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump path to erasing hush money conviction
articles.summary: A three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision on November 23, moving Donald Trump's hush money criminal conviction case to a federal court. The ruling allows Trump to argue for the verdict's dismissal on presidential immunity grounds. Trump was convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in New York.
articles.description: The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court; if that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity

articles.headline: United States targets Iranian shadow banking networks with new sanctions
articles.title: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks
articles.summary: The United States Department of the Treasury announced sanctions on November 24 targeting more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel under Operation Economic Outcast. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated the measures aim to disrupt financial lifelines used by Tehran. The Central Bank of Iran oversees the designated entities, which facilitate foreign currency transactions despite comprehensive sanctions.
articles.description: US Treasury sanctions over two dozen Iranian entities, citing efforts to disrupt Tehran's global financial activities.

articles.title: US states sue SpaceX over Grok AI’s creation of child sexual abuse material
articles.summary: The states of Virginia and Oregon filed lawsuits in state courts against Elon Musk's SpaceX on November 24, alleging the company misled consumers and removed safeguards on its Grok artificial intelligence chatbot. The attorneys general accused SpaceX of violating consumer protection laws by enabling the generation of sexualized images and child sexual abuse material through its spicy mode feature.
articles.description: Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits on Monday, accusing the company of promoting Grok's 'spicy mode'.

articles.headline: Climate negotiations stall in Antalya as power-hungry artificial intelligence data centers surge
articles.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
articles.summary: Delegates at the United Nations climate conference, designated COP31, failed to pass a final pact in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday as discussions collapsed over energy commitments and emissions. Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence data centers complicated global transition goals, with companies like Meta and Google reporting increased carbon footprints and voluntary pledges struggling to secure sufficient international backing.
articles.description: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It's a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday. articles.headline: UK sanctions five Myanmar military leaders following Rohingya genocide ruling
articles.title: UK sanctions top Myanmar military leaders after Rohingya genocide ruling
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice ruled that the state committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the measures, alongside plans to halt aviation fuel supplies. The 2017 military crackdown killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 refugees to flee into Bangladesh.
articles.description: The UK is joined by several other nations in recognising an ICJ ruling that Myanmar carried out genocide.

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Russian corvette in Libya amid widening war
articles.title: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces successfully targeted a Russian navy corvette anchored inside a Mediterranean harbour in Benghazi, Libya. The SBU intelligence operation drew swift condemnation from Moscow and the United Nations. The incident highlights the expanding geographical scope of the conflict as Russian and Ukrainian forces increasingly engage in hybrid and drone warfare across Europe and beyond.
articles.description: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.

articles.headline: Indian Parliament Winter Session history remains rare
articles.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
articles.summary: The Winter Session of the Indian Parliament has been skipped only four times throughout history, typically due to exceptional events like the Emergency or the COVID-19 pandemic. With the Monsoon Session remaining unprorogued for over 100 days, speculation has emerged regarding a potential special session to address the delimitation Bill, though no official confirmation has been provided.
articles.description: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic

articles.description: Moscow accuses Tallinn of 'hostile actions' citing border closure and claiming it is allowing Ukraine to launch attacks.

articles.title: India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modi
articles.summary: India announced a $1.62 billion economic package to support Nepal following devastating August floods that killed over 1,300 people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah confirmed the aid, which includes grants for infrastructure and credit for energy projects. The funding aims to assist reconstruction efforts after glacial collapses caused widespread destruction.
articles.description: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is in New Delhi for a two-day visit — his first since coming to power in March.

articles.headline: Netherlands Foreign Minister calls for international rule of law
articles.title: Rule of law needed, not ‘Rule of Power’: Netherlands Foreign Minister Berendsen on trilateral summit
articles.summary: Netherlands Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen urged India and European nations to strengthen partnerships based on the international rule of law. Speaking during a visit to India, Berendsen suggested that these countries should act as a counterweight to the rule of power demonstrated by major nations during the recent trilateral summit held in Shenzhen, China.
articles.description: Berendsen holds talks with EAM Jaishankar, says Europe and India must end dependencies on global powers for energy, security and technology

articles.headline: Tajikistan notifies United Nations of its decision to withdraw from International Criminal Court
articles.title: Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against court
articles.summary: Tajikistan formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, becoming the fourth nation to initiate departure since the United States urged countries to leave in July. The withdrawal from the Rome Statute will take effect on November 20, 2027. The International Criminal Court expressed concern following the announcement by the Central Asian nation.
articles.description: The ICC found that Tajikistan failed to comply with its request to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses over fossil fuel language
articles.title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
articles.summary: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an agreement after nations failed to reach a consensus on fossil fuel commitments. While roughly 130 countries demanded explicit language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, opposition from oil-producing nations and disagreements over climate finance prevented a final deal. The summit highlighted deep geopolitical divisions regarding climate action.
articles.description: Interests of oil-producing countries, a US boycott and a dispute over finance may have torpedoed climate talks.

articles.headline: Houthi officials report 17 deaths in Saudi-led coalition attack on Hodeida
articles.title: 17 killed in Saudi attack on Yemeni city: Houthis
articles.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement reported that a Saudi-led coalition airstrike killed 17 workers and destroyed telecommunications facilities in Hodeida on November 23, 2026. The group’s Telecommunications Ministry stated the attack disrupted internet services for thousands. Separately, Houthis claimed a coalition strike in Lahj caused further casualties. Saudi Arabia has not commented on the reported incidents.
articles.description: Coalition airstrikes on telecoms facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more, and caused the “total destruction” of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other sites, the Houthis’ Telecommunications Ministry said

articles.headline: Oxfam report warns Israeli military attacks have contaminated Gaza environment
articles.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
articles.summary: A comprehensive report by Oxfam International and the Conflict and Environment Observatory reveals that Israeli military operations have severely contaminated the Palestinian territory with heavy metals, asbestos and untreated sewage. Amitabh Behar, executive director of Oxfam International, condemned the destruction as environmental war crimes. The Israeli government has previously rejected genocide accusations at the International Court of Justice, maintaining that its campaign is a self-defence measure against Hamas.
articles.description: The report says there are signs of possible contamination across almost all of Gaza as a result of Israel's actions.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy claims Ukrainian drone attack sank Russian warship in Libya
articles.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on November 23, 2026, that maritime drones sank the Russian navy corvette Merkury at a port in Benghazi, Libya. Libyan officials confirmed the vessel was struck by drones on November 22, 2026, causing significant damage. Russia’s Defense Ministry has not provided a formal response regarding the status of the ship.
articles.description: The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill United Nations relief worker and two others in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including United Nations Relief and Works Agency worker Adel al-Helo in the Jabalia refugee camp. A separate strike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two individuals. The attacks occurred despite an October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas that halted major combat operations.
articles.description: Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 'ceasefire' deal.

Trump stated he believed Huang should return, citing national security assessments that found no evidence of unlawful conduct. Nvidia’s board confirmed they received input from senior U.S. government officials before finalizing the decision to rehire Huang.
articles.description: It sure looked like President Donald Trump played a role in Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO - and now the White House is making sure everyone knows he was. articles.headline: Moscow warns Ukraine of consequences after drone attacks on Russian vessels
articles.title: Russia warns Ukraine of ‘dangerous trend’ after Libya and Baltic attacks
articles.summary: Moscow warned Ukraine of painful consequences following drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya and the Baltic Sea, which Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov described as a dangerous trend. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that his forces sank two ships, including the corvette Merkury in Benghazi. In response to maritime transit vulnerabilities, Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin announced plans to spend 47 billion roubles on rail ferries.
articles.description: Russia has reacted with fury to Ukraine's continued campaign targeting its naval and merchant shipping.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following revelations of two affairs
articles.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset and another with an Nvidia colleague. The departure creates uncertainty for the chipmaker, which is central to the artificial intelligence sector and valued at nearly $4 trillion. Despite previous backing from United States President Donald Trump, the board accepted his resignation following the disclosures.
articles.description: Days after resigning while mired in scandal of extra-marital affairs, Nvidia's Jensen Huang is making a remarkable return.

articles.headline: Explosion damages Russian ship at Benghazi naval base in Libya
articles.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
articles.summary: An explosion occurred on a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base port following a suspected drone attack, according to Libya's eastern government. The incident happened at dawn while the vessel was stopping for fuel and supplies, prompting a joint investigation between local authorities and Russian counterparts.
articles.description: The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy urges immediate four-way peace talks involving Russia and European leaders
articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for urgent four-party negotiations between Ukraine, Russia, the United States, and Europe during a NATO Parliamentary Assembly meeting in Berlin on November 23, 2026. Zelenskyy also reiterated his demand for Ukraine to join NATO, though Secretary General Mark Rutte noted that alliance members currently lack the unanimous support required.
articles.description: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

articles.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive officer
articles.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO on November 23, 2026, just over a week after his resignation. The decision followed government assurances regarding national security and sparked a 33 percent rise in company shares. Despite the return, Huang remains under investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Justice.
articles.description: Huang stepped down earlier this month after revelations of at least two affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy.

articles.headline: Vina Nadjibulla says Modi visit will reset Canada relations
articles.title: Modi’s Canada visit is set to move ties in a new direction: Vina Nadjibulla
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's upcoming visit to Canada provides a vital opportunity to reset bilateral relations. According to Vina Nadjibulla, co-founder and chief executive officer of the Centre for Strategic Statecraft, both countries have achieved significant progress in normalizing diplomatic ties following a recent breakdown in communication between Ottawa and New Delhi.
articles.description: What has changed is that both governments appear increasingly willing to approach security issues through the lens of mutual security interests, rather than allowing these differences to define the entire relationship, says CEO of the Vancouver-based think tank

articles.headline: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal to strengthen bilateral ties
articles.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
articles.summary: India has announced a $1.6bn support package for Nepal to bolster diplomatic relations and assist with post-flood reconstruction. The funding includes energy project credit and infrastructure grants. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart, Balen Shah, also inaugurated a cross-border train service and secured new port access to improve connectivity between the two nations.
articles.description: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.

articles.headline: Iran vows to counter US naval blockade with all available means
articles.title: Iran says it will use ‘all available means’ to counter US blockade
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated on Monday that Tehran will use all necessary measures to challenge the US naval blockade. The blockade, restored in July following a collapsed agreement, has severely impacted Iran's oil exports. Iran maintains that the US actions constitute military aggression and claims it is entitled to self-defense under international law.
articles.description: Ministry of Foreign Affairs says Iran will use all tools to confront the naval siege and defend itself.

articles.headline: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992 following North Carolina victory
articles.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
articles.summary: The Democratic Party achieved its biggest House majority since 1992 after Chuck Hubbard defeated incumbent Republican Representative Virginia Foxx by 330 votes in North Carolina. The race was officially called on November 23, 2026, following a recount requested by Foxx. Hubbard campaigned heavily on local economic issues and the rising cost of living associated with the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
articles.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

articles.title: COP31 ends without a deal: Is global climate diplomacy breaking? | The Hindu Analysis
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit held in Antalya, Türkiye, concluded without reaching an agreement on a final cover text. The deadlock stemmed from sharp disagreements among participating nations regarding fossil fuels, climate finance, and emissions reductions, raising questions about the future direction of international climate diplomacy and the Paris Agreement.

articles.headline: Supreme Court criticizes Bihar judge for convicting police superintendent
articles.title: ‘Stop acting like Baahubali,’ says Supreme Court to Bihar judicial officer for FIR against Superintendent of Police
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, criticized a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a Superintendent of Police over an unexecuted order to register a first information report. articles.description: A Bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana questioned Bihar Judge Anil Kumar’s conduct and said his understanding of law is appalling

articles.headline: Global powers compete for mineral wealth across the African continent
articles.title: How the US, China and Russia are competing for Africa’s mineral wealth
articles.summary: The United States, China, and Russia are competing fiercely for Africa's critical mineral wealth, including cobalt in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and lithium in Mali. While Beijing dominates supply chains through investments and the Belt and Road Initiative, Washington and Moscow are deploying diplomatic, economic, and security partnerships to secure strategic resources.

articles.title: Markets take heavy drubbing dragged by banks; Sensex plunges 1,484 points, Nifty dives to 25,349.65

The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 1,483.72 points to settle at 82,435.99, while the NSE Nifty slid below 25,350. Heavy selling pressure across banking, financial services, and metal stocks dragged the indices down significantly from earlier highs.

articles.headline: Ukraine reports drone strikes on Russian vessels near Libya
articles.title: Ukraine shares video of strikes on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky released footage on Sunday appearing to show Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian ships off the Libyan coast. The attack reportedly sank a warship and damaged a cargo vessel allegedly transporting weapons. While the Kremlin warned of regional escalation, it did not directly address the incident, and local health officials confirmed receiving injured personnel.
articles.description: President Zelensky said a Russia warship was sunk, with a Russian cargo ship also hit.

articles.title: COP31: What next after UN climate talks collapse
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya concluded in failure after participating nations deadlocked over phasing out fossil fuels and financing energy transitions for developing countries. The conference collapsed on Sunday as the European Union and vulnerable nations rejected a draft agreement supported by oil-producing states. Delegates and experts warned that the stalemate highlights persistent divisions and raises questions regarding the consensus-based negotiation process under the United Nations.
articles.description: UN member states fail to agree on how to fast-track action to reverse global warming in a blow to climate agenda.

articles.headline: Ukraine claims responsibility for naval drone attacks on Russian vessels
articles.title: Ukraine claims drone strikes on Russian ships off Libya: What do we know?
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and struck the cargo vessel MV Angara off the coast of Libya. The operation forms part of an ongoing military campaign targeting Moscow naval assets and cargo ships linked to shadow fleets. Meanwhile, the United Nations Support Mission in Libya expressed serious concern over the incident and called for an immediate independent investigation into the attacks.
articles.description: Drone strikes on two Russian vessels near Libyan coast fuels fears of Ukraine war's spread.

articles.headline: US congressional panel urges dialogue with India on Dalai Lama succession
articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.summary: A bipartisan United States congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level diplomatic and intelligence channel with India to plan for the 14th Dalai Lama's succession. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission warned that China might turn the reincarnation process into an international legitimacy contest, while urging the recognition of the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority.
articles.description: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

articles.headline: India and China hold second round of military talks in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why the second round of Corps Commander-level dialogue in Arunachal Pradesh matters
articles.summary: India and China held nearly ten days of Corps Commander-level discussions in Arunachal Pradesh beginning on November 8, 2026, aimed at preventing border tensions along the Line of Actual Control. Lieutenant General Girish Kalia led the Indian delegation alongside a Ministry of External Affairs official during the talks, which focused on addressing competing territorial claims and ongoing military challenges in the Eastern Sector.
articles.description: The second round is aimed at establishing clearer engagement protocols between the two armies, preventing face-offs between patrol parties from escalating into larger confrontations and ensuring that communication channels remain open

articles.headline: Grameen Bank branches targeted in Bangladesh amid political unrest
articles.title: Why is Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank under attack?
articles.summary: Grameen Bank recorded 97 attacks on its branches and offices between November 10 and 23, according to internal memorandums. Managing director Sarder Akhter Hamed confirmed that attackers looted documents and destroyed records. Government officials and researchers attribute the violence to supporters of the ousted Awami League directing anger at founder Muhammad Yunus following the removal of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from power in August 2024.
articles.description: Leading financial institution has found itself at centre of tensions amid violence by Sheikh Hasina supporters.

articles.headline: Palestinian landowners face severe access restrictions in West Bank military zones.
articles.title: Occupied West Bank ‘military zones’ become de facto Israeli settler land
articles.summary: Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank face severe restrictions in accessing their ancestral lands after military zones and farm outposts effectively block their entry. Property owners report widespread destruction, theft and violence by Israeli settlers. Legal experts and human rights organisations note that such closures increasingly hand over territory to settlers despite official legal protections for local farmers.
articles.description: Closed military zones in the occupied West Bank are being seized by settlers as staging posts for pogroms.

articles.headline: India announces development package worth over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal
articles.title: India announces development package over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal’s development

articles.description: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM

articles.title: At least 15 killed in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as Russia intensifies attacks

articles.headline: Oxfam report blames Israel for toxic pollution across majority of Gaza.
articles.title: ‘Environmental crimes’: Israel blamed for toxic pollution in 99% of Gaza
articles.summary: A report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory states that Israeli military operations have contaminated over ninety-nine percent of Gaza, creating a toxic wasteland with severe risks to human life.
