articles.summary: In a historic ruling, the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya during military clearance operations in Rakhine State in 2017. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate perpetrators, ensure non-repetition, and allow the safe return of displaced persons. The final judgment resulted from a case brought by The Gambia in 2019.
articles.description: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

articles.headline: Israeli soldiers assault Palestinian after raiding his home
articles.title: Israeli soldiers assault Palestinian after raiding his home
articles.description: Israeli forces assault a Palestinian man during a raid on his home in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Tajikistan begins process of withdrawing from International Criminal Court
articles.title: Tajikistan becomes fourth country to withdraw from International Criminal Court
articles.summary: Tajikistan has formally started withdrawing from the International Criminal Court, becoming the fourth nation to initiate the exit process since July following a United States diplomatic push. The ICC governing body stated on November 23, 2026, that the departure risks undermining global justice, following prior criticism over Tajikistan failing to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, ‌denouncing the Court as an instrument of "neocolonial ​repression"

articles.headline: Police investigate anonymous bomb threats targeting schools across Germany and Denmark
articles.title: Police investigating bomb threats against schools in Germany and Denmark
articles.summary: Authorities in Germany and Denmark are investigating emailed bomb threats that affected approximately 450 schools across German states including Berlin, Baden-Wurttemberg, and Thuringia, as well as Copenhagen. Police concluded that the warnings lacked a concrete danger and were not serious hoaxes intended to cause fear. Interior ministry officials stated that institutions were not advised to evacuate during the incidents.
articles.description: Bomb threats follow hoax emails sent to schools across Europe earlier in November.

articles.headline: Mexican soldiers attacked by drug cartel members following leader's arrest
articles.title: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
articles.summary: Mexican soldiers patrolling in Sinaloa de Leyva were targeted in a deadly shootout by cartel members on Sunday, following the arrest of cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores on Friday. According to the Mexican defence ministry, four soldiers and 16 criminals died in the violence. The operation involved special forces and was supported by United States agencies.
articles.description: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.

articles.headline: Hyderabad Police investigate bomb threat email sent via Europe-based VPN
articles.title: Hyderabad bomb threat email sender used Europe-based VPN, temporary email account
articles.summary: Cybercrime teams are analyzing digital trails after Hyderabad Police received a threat email on November 21, 2026, warning of attacks at Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza. The sender used a Europe-based virtual private network and a temporary account. Officials intensified security across public locations, and citizens were urged to report suspicious items by dialing 112.
articles.description: Cybercrime teams are working to trace the sender of the threatening email, which warned of 26/11-style attacks and named Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as targets

articles.headline: Displaced Palestinians protest in Gaza as Israeli strikes and home destructions continue
articles.title: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
articles.summary: Hundreds of displaced residents demonstrated near Deir el-Balah to protest against intensifying air strikes and property destructions by Israeli forces beyond the Yellow Line established under a ceasefire. According to local officials, recent attacks have left hundreds of thousands homeless, while continuing military operations and recent strikes have caused numerous casualties across the enclave.
articles.description: Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a 'gradual displacement' policy, a Gaza mayor says.

articles.headline: Israeli restrictions cut off vital hearing aid supplies in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli restrictions cut off vital hearing aid supplies in Gaza
articles.description: Israeli restrictions have left Gaza facing a severe shortage of hearing aid batteries.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India retains three major banks in 2026 D-SIB list
articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has maintained State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank in its 2026 domestic systemically important banks list. Based on data from March 31, 2026, the institutions remain under their previous bucketing structures, requiring additional capital buffers of up to 0.80 percent to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.
articles.description: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

articles.headline: National strike causes transport disruption across Belgium amid government budget crisis
articles.title: Anti-austerity strike spurs transport chaos across Belgium
articles.summary: Trade unions organized a national strike across Belgium on Monday, causing widespread disruption to public transport, schools, and flights. Air traffic control agency Skeyes halted services, forcing Brussels and Charleroi airports to cancel departures. The walkout protests federal government austerity measures led by Prime Minister Bart De Wever, who faces a December deadline to resolve a budget impasse.
articles.description: National strike against planned austerity causes widespread disruption, with government's fate hanging in the balance.

articles.headline: India automobile retail sales reach record 55.25 lakh units during festive season
articles.title: Auto retail hits record 55.25 lakh units during 42-day festive season, EV sales suge 53%: FADA
articles.summary: Automobile retail sales in India grew 2.21 percent year-on-year to a record 55,25,490 units during the 42-day festive season, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations. Electric vehicle adoption surged 52.62 percent to surpass five lakh units. Passenger vehicle sales declined by 7.16 percent, while two-wheelers, three-wheelers, commercial vehicles, tractors, and construction equipment all registered growth.
articles.description: Compared with the festive season of 2024, vehicle retail sales registered a growth of 23.95%, indicating sustained demand momentum following the GST rate rationalisation

articles.headline: Thousands march in Lisbon to protest soaring living costs and housing crisis
articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.summary: Thousands of individuals participated in a central Lisbon march on November 21, 2026, organised by trade union federation CGTP to protest against increasing living costs, low wages, and a severe housing crisis. Protesters demanded higher wages and lower prices. Portugal faces high inflation and surging property prices, compounding economic pressures experienced by workers and younger generations across the country.
articles.description: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

articles.headline: Mexican special forces arrest top FBI most-wanted drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores
articles.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
articles.summary: Mexican special forces detained alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa, following a shoot-out involving gunfire and explosives. Meza Flores, leader of the Meza Flores Organisation and on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was flown to Mexico City to face extradition and prosecution. The operation occurred amid increased Mexican efforts to combat cartels under US pressure.
articles.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

articles.headline: France faces social unrest and protests amid severe economic challenges
articles.title: 'I want to destroy capitalism, not France': On the streets with the French ultra left
articles.summary: The text cuts off abruptly before presenting the full news report, providing only the beginning of an article about social unrest, political tensions, and protests in France.
articles.description: The BBC meets the far-left protesters French President Emmanuel Macron says are trying to bring down the Republic.

articles.headline: Tata Sons postpones crucial board meeting to November 30 following Noel Tata objections
articles.title: Tata Sons board meet postponed to November 30 after Noel raises concerns
articles.summary: Tata Sons delayed its scheduled board meeting from November 26 to November 30, 2026, after Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata raised concerns over inadequate notice. The upcoming session will address the Reserve Bank of India mandated public listing, potential corporate restructuring alternatives, and financial support for the Shapoorji Pallonji Group.
articles.description: The crucial meeting on November 30 will discuss items including the RBI-mandated listing of Tata Sons or ways forward on complying with the central bank's requests, they said.

articles.headline: Edappadi K. Palaniswami moves to consolidate control over AIADMK party.
articles.title: Palaniswami seeks to consolidate his hold over AIADMK
articles.summary: All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami rejected reconciliation with dissident factions and sidelined former minister S.P. Velumani ahead of an anticipated general council meeting. Palaniswami aims to ratify recent disciplinary actions following internal party rebellions and recent electoral setbacks. While senior figures urge flexibility to improve party fortunes, loyalists defend the leadership's current stance.
articles.description: The AIADMK general secretary may seek ratification of his disciplinary action against rebels during the general council meeting to be held soon

articles.headline: Congress accuses government of diminishing Parliament dignity over session uncertainty
articles.title: Modi government is diminishing dignity of Parliament: Congress
articles.summary: The Congress party accused the central government on November 23, 2026, of undermining parliamentary dignity by failing to prorogue the Monsoon Session or announce dates for the Winter Session. According to party leaders Jairam Ramesh and Shashi Tharoor, the ongoing uncertainty creates unnecessary disruption for lawmakers and suggests the administration may be concealing deliberate political motives.
articles.description: Jairam Ramesh said the country was entitled to know the government’s formula for delimitation, after what he described as its efforts to cobble together a “super-tainted two-thirds majority” in the Lok Sabha

articles.headline: Nigerian rescue teams search for survivors after overcrowded boat capsizes
articles.title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
articles.summary: Nigerian rescue teams are searching for survivors after an overcrowded boat carrying funeral mourners capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State. The National Emergency Management Agency reported that 29 bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued. President Bola Tinubu directed disaster response agencies to assist, while officials ordered stricter enforcement of waterway safety standards.
articles.description: The government blames overcrowding, poor maintenance, and missing life jackets for boat accidents.

articles.headline: Clashes erupt across France in another night of protest
articles.title: Clashes erupt across France in another night of protest
articles.description: French police charged to disperse crowds on Saturday as the country faced a sixth weekend of demonstrations.

articles.headline: FSSAI suspends licences of five nutraceutical and health product manufacturers
articles.title: FSSAI suspends licences of 5 nutraceutical, health product manufacturers
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India announced on November 23, 2026, that it has suspended the operational licences of five nutraceutical and health product companies. The regulatory action targets Vedant Remedies, Lucid Healthcare Private Limited, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals, and Adorreal Healthcare due to serious infractions, including poor hygiene standards and damaged infrastructure.
articles.description: The six companies against whom the action was initiated are Airen Herbals, Aquabliss Lifesciences, Raskam Healthcare, Supercure Biotech, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare and Vedant Remedies

articles.headline: Government warns public against security risks of leaving WhatsApp Web logged in
articles.title: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warns of possible misuse of WhatsApp Web sessions
articles.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre issued an advisory on November 18, 2026, cautioning users about security risks when using WhatsApp Web on shared systems. According to the Home Ministry's anti-cybercrime wing, active sessions left open on public computers can be hijacked for fraud or impersonation. Officials recommended manually logging out after every session and avoiding sensitive work on untrusted devices.
articles.description: National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit issues advisory asking users to manually log out after every session

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet orders forfeiture of copies of Ravi Hanj book Basava Mantapa
articles.title: Is forfeiting copies of a book the right way to handle ‘objectionable content’?
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet decided to forfeit copies of the book Basava Mantapa by NRI author Ravi Hanj over alleged derogatory remarks about social reformer Basavanna, reigniting debate over freedom of expression and public order. This marks at least the sixth book banned or forfeited in the state since independence following protests by religious or caste groups over hurt sentiments.
articles.description: The Constitution provides for a ban or forfeiture of a book on three grounds - national security, threat to public order and threat to public morality

articles.headline: BJP chief Nitin Nabin criticises Rahul Gandhi over vote theft allegations
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi advocates for votes of infiltrators, says BJP chief Nitin Nabin
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party president Nitin Nabin criticised opposition leader Rahul Gandhi during a political rally in Karimnagar on November 23, 2026. Responding to allegations concerning vote irregularities, the Bharatiya Janata Party leader claimed that the senior Congress figure promotes the interests of infiltrators and damages India's reputation while operating alongside the Telangana Chief Minister.
articles.description: Nitin Nabin, addressing a rally in Telangana to counter the ‘vote chori’ (vote theft) narrative of Congress, also said Rahul Gandhi insults the country on foreign soil

articles.headline: Delhi police considered reporter vests to distinguish journalists during protests
articles.title: Delhi Police considered reporter jackets, press IDs to distinguish journalists from ‘reel-makers’ during anti-SIR protests
articles.summary: Delhi Police evaluated issuing specialised high-visibility vests and distinct identification cards during October demonstrations to separate accredited journalists from social media content creators. Senior officers noted that proposals were ultimately abandoned due to security replication risks, while law enforcement officials subsequently defended distinguishing individuals based on their conduct during public protests.
articles.description: Fake press cards, protesters posing as mediapersons and confusion over journalistic credentials complicated crowd management; police dropped the proposed identification measures over fears they could be replicated.

articles.headline: Indian rupee falls 30 paise to settle at 92.92 against U.S. dollar
articles.title: Rupee snaps 5-day rally; tumbles 30 paise to settle at 92.92 against U.S. dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee declined 30 paise to close at 92.92 against the U.S. dollar on November 23, 2026, breaking a five-day winning streak due to heavy selling in domestic stock markets. According to forex traders, the local currency faced volatility as the Sensex and Nifty crashed over one percent each, despite easing crude oil prices and a softening American currency supporting the downside.
articles.description: Lower crude oil prices and a softening American currency failed to support the local currency, which faced intense volatility amid a global stock market rout, forex traders said

articles.headline: Bangladesh garment makers propose 15 percent wage increase amid ongoing industry protests
articles.title: Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand
articles.summary: Apparel manufacturers in Bangladesh plan to suggest a roughly 15 percent minimum wage increase during authority talks on November 23, 2026. This falls well short of employee demands for 30,000 taka compared to the current 12,500 taka. Unrest has caused millions in losses as global brands and labour groups urge meaningful pay raises to address soaring living costs.
articles.description: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs

articles.headline: Federal Bureau of Investigation investigates apparent hack of criminal information database
articles.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center database, according to United States media reports citing two briefed sources. The database is utilized by law enforcement agencies to share information regarding warrants and background checks. This development follows recent high-profile cybersecurity incidents and the firing of White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.
articles.description: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

articles.headline: French government meets student protesters as demonstrations over education conditions continue
articles.title: Inside the talks between student protest leaders and Macron’s government
articles.summary: French high school students have held multiple meetings with top officials including President Emmanuel Macron and Education Minister Edouard Geffray following months of nationwide protests. Demonstrators demand an overhaul of the Parcoursup university admissions platform, increased teacher staffing, and an emergency renovation plan to address severely dilapidated school infrastructure.
articles.description: Al Jazeera interviews two French student leaders who have met with top government officials as protests continue.

articles.headline: U.S. Commerce Department issues interim rule restricting advanced AI chip exports
articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on November 16, 2026, barring foreign data centers with American AI chips from providing cloud services to businesses in twenty-four countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. China criticized the move as an overreach of national security, while the policy builds on export controls established in 2018.
articles.description: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

articles.headline: Kerala police investigate fairness cream linked to severe kidney ailment in teenager
articles.title: Police investigate fairness cream's alleged link to Indian teen's kidney ailment
articles.summary: Police in Kerala, India, and the child rights commission have registered cases against an uncertified fairness cream manufacturer after a 17-year-old girl developed membranous nephropathy. Laboratory tests revealed the product contained mercury levels thousands of times above permissible limits, prompting urgent medical treatment and renewed scrutiny of unregulated skin-lightening products.
articles.description: Doctors who treated the 17-year-old girl say that the cream allegedly contained toxic levels of mercury.

articles.headline: Lebanese president demands Israeli withdrawal and condemns Iranian interference
articles.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
articles.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun criticized Iranian meddling and demanded a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon in a speech ahead of the country's independence anniversary. According to authorities, ongoing Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon have killed thousands of people since fighting began. Aoun also pledged to bring all armed groups under state control.
articles.description: Joseph Aoun says 'two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked' mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.

articles.headline: India captain Shubman Gill defends Mohammed Siraj omission during drawn New Zealand Test
articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Siraj’s omission was a difficult decision, says skipper Shubman
articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill stated that leaving Mohammed Siraj out of the playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand was a difficult personal choice dictated by current form. Gill also defended the decision to settle for a draw on November 23, 2026, citing heavy workloads for fast bowlers and unresponsive pitch conditions.
articles.description: ‘Even before playing for India, we were really good friends, so leaving him behind was actually a very tough decision for me as well,’ Shubman Gill said

articles.headline: Climate change remains an existential crisis despite geopolitical distractions, says Katrin Jakobsdottir
articles.title: Former Icelandic PM says world’s great powers are flexing their muscles
articles.summary: Former Icelandic Prime Minister Katrin Jakobsdottir warns that climate change remains a critical existential threat and security emergency even as global power politics sidelines environmental action. Speaking about her home country where the Arctic is warming rapidly and glaciers are retreating, she stresses that the warming world demands urgent attention while major global powers flex their military and political muscles.
articles.description: Iceland’s former PM warns climate change remains an existential threat as global power politics sidelines action.

articles.headline: Walmart integrates Meta Muse to enable AI agent shopping for Black Friday
articles.title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
articles.summary: Walmart announced that Meta Platforms Inc.'s AI agent Muse will be permitted to browse and purchase Black Friday deals on its website through a new Agent Gateway. According to the retail giant, the system uses dedicated Agent Profiles that allow customers to set spending limits and approve purchases. The rollout was delayed by twenty-four hours to begin on November 24, 2026.
articles.description: Walmart will now let Meta's Muse shop on your behalf, allowing the AI agent to find and purchase Black Friday deals via Walmart's Sparky AI assistant. The retail giant is rolling out a live implementation of the Agent Gateway it announced last month, which helps AI agents find relevant products for you without sharing your […]

articles.headline: Former Vice-President Hamid Ansari warns of growing authoritarian rule in India
articles.title: India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari
articles.summary: Former Vice-President Hamid Ansari stated that India is gradually shifting towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions. Speaking via a video message at a Kolkata seminar on November 22, 2026, he highlighted a threefold challenge involving neoliberal economic policies and communal polarisation. Other speakers at the event included CPI-M general secretary M.A. Baby and Cuban Ambassador Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera.
articles.description: Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, economist Prabhat Patanaik spoke at a seminar titled ‘The new age of imperialism’ organised by Sitaram Yechury foundation

articles.headline: Lebanese families return to ruins after Israeli attacks in south
articles.title: Lebanese families return to ruins after Israeli attacks in south
articles.description: In southern Lebanon’s Nabatieh, displaced families have been returning to ruins and widespread destruction.

articles.headline: China expresses readiness to facilitate visa arrangements for Indian business personnel
articles.title: China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people
articles.summary: China stated it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides amid reports of reduced visa issuance by Chinese diplomatic missions. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson responded on November 23, 2026, to inquiries regarding restrictions. This development follows recent efforts by both nations to normalise bilateral ties and promote travel cooperation.
articles.description: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

articles.headline: India claims two wickets before lunch on final day against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ first Test Day 5: New Zealand batters blunt Indian attack; match ends in draw
articles.summary: India capitalized on favorable wind conditions to dismiss Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra during the opening session of the final day in the first Test match at Basin Reserve. Spinner Washington Sundar and fast bowler Prasidh Krishna secured the breakthroughs, leaving New Zealand trailing by 195 runs at lunch. Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell managed to steady the innings before the interval, keeping the visitors at bay as play continued.
articles.description: The hosts blunted to near-perfection, the teams shook hands at the beginning of the last 15 overs, with New Zealand placed at 239 for five

articles.headline: Asean and India convene in Visakhapatnam to secure Indo-Pacific maritime trade routes
articles.title: ASEAN-India Maritime Conclave in Visakhapatnam calls for deeper cooperation to secure Indo-Pacific trade routes
articles.summary: Policymakers and naval officials gathered in Visakhapatnam for the two-day Association of Southeast Asian Nations and India Maritime Conclave, which began on November 23, 2026. Organised by the India Foundation and the Ministry of External Affairs, the event focused on regional security, blue economies, and trade resilience. Leaders emphasised cooperative measures to counter maritime threats across the Indo-Pacific region.
articles.description: Nara Lokesh pitches Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km coastline as an industrial and digital gateway for ASEAN supply chains

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit deadlocked over fossil fuel reduction references
articles.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
articles.summary: Negotiations at the COP31 United Nations climate summit in Turkey entered a deadlock after a group of nations led by France and Panama opposed a draft agreement omitting references to reducing fossil fuel demand. Disagreements also persist over funding for adaptation, with African nations demanding increased financial support. A new agreement is anticipated as discussions continue among participating international ministers.
articles.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

articles.headline: The Hindu Group publishes e-book examining post-election strategic landscape in Israel
articles.title: Israel at an Inflection Point
articles.summary: The Hindu Group has released an e-book titled Israel at an Inflection Point, exploring the domestic and geopolitical transformations in Israel following recent Knesset elections and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu losing his majority. The publication features essays by scholars analyzing the aftermath of the October 7 Hamas attacks, ongoing regional conflicts involving Iran, and India's evolving diplomatic balance in West Asia.
articles.description: The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation

articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack hits industrial facility
articles.description: Bahrain says Iranian attack hits industrial facility

articles.title: Thousands displaced after deadly storm hits Brazil town
articles.description: A powerful supercell storm devastated the Brazilian town of Tupancireta.

articles.headline: Bahrain reports industrial facility fire following Iranian aerial attack
articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial facility
articles.summary: Bahrain announced that an Iranian aerial attack struck a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries, according to the Bahrain Defence Force and the Ministry of Interior. Meanwhile, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it targeted United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in response to airspace violations. The incident occurred amid escalating regional conflict involving Gulf Arab states and Iran.
articles.description: Bahrain reports no injuries as Iran's IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.

articles.headline: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot invites Likud party for coalition talks
articles.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming the next Israeli government, invited caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party for coalition talks beginning on Sunday, November 22, 2026. The centrist Yashar party leader stated the meetings reflect a commitment to forming a broad government. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett expressed opposition to joining Netanyahu's bloc.
articles.description: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

articles.headline: Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang warns artificial superintelligence is arriving
articles.title: Artificial superintelligence ‘arriving’, warns top Meta executive
articles.summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang warned on Sunday that artificial superintelligence surpassing human intellect is imminent and could lead humanity to lose control. Speaking after an Anthropic employee used AI to solve a complex mathematical problem, Wang emphasized the urgent need for safety and security measures to ensure technology empowers rather than overtakes society.
articles.description: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang says humankind's actions over next year will have 'great consequence' for the world.

articles.headline: Indian man jailed over plot to kill Sikh separatist in US
articles.title: Indian man jailed over plot to kill Sikh separatist in US
articles.description: An Indian national has been sentenced to more than 19 years in a US prison for plotting to assassinate Sikh separatist.

articles.headline: Delhi minister states sixty percent of Yamuna river is cleaned
articles.title: Yamuna 60% clean, water safe to drink; entire river to be cleaned by 2030: Delhi Minister Sirsa
articles.summary: Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa stated on November 23, 2026, that sixty percent of the Yamuna river has been cleaned and its water is now potable. Speaking at an event in New Delhi, he credited Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and the Union government for the progress, noting that sewage treatment plants are being used to clean the entire river by 2030.
articles.description: “60% of Yamuna jii is totally clean… Clean means so clean that even you can drink that water,” Delhi Minister Sirsa said, urging people to visit the river and see for themselves

articles.headline: Iran urges US to accept conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
articles.summary: Iranian officials met with Qatari mediators in Tehran to discuss terms for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Washington must accept conditions including the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the economic blockade before shipping lanes can be restored following the conflict that began on February 28.
articles.description: Iran's foreign minister says reopening the strait is 'not difficult' if the US accepts reasonable conditions.

articles.headline: Widowed amid war and displacement: Sudanese mothers struggle to survive
articles.title: Widowed amid war and displacement: Sudanese mothers struggle to survive
articles.description: War widows in Sudan face growing challenges supporting their children as the cost of living increases.

articles.headline: Kenya and Democratic Republic of Congo agree to restore full diplomatic ties
articles.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
articles.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto and Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi agreed to restore full diplomatic relations during a Sunday summit in Oyo, Congo-Brazzaville. Relations had deteriorated after Democratic Republic of Congo accused Kenya of hosting rebel leaders. Facilitated by Denis Sassou Nguesso, the leaders also discussed regional integration, trade cooperation, and managing the ongoing Ebola virus outbreak.
articles.description: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".

articles.headline: Supreme Court restricts Tamil Nadu from taking coercive action against SASTRA University
articles.title: Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court restrained the Tamil Nadu government from executing coercive measures against SASTRA University in Thanjavur regarding disputed land. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant directed the State to file a response after senior advocates noted the administration rejected an alternative land proposal, insisting instead on reclaiming the thirty one point three seven acres used for public education.
articles.description: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly encroached upon by the Thanjavur university

articles.headline: Cartel leader arrest triggers deadly violence across northern Mexico
articles.title: 11 killed in burst of violence in northern Mexico after capture of cartel leader Meza Flores
articles.summary: At least eleven people were killed during clashes in Guasave after Mexican forces captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores. The Defense Cabinet reported that seven alleged gunmen and four soldiers died in the violence. The operation relied on intelligence from the United States administration and led to widespread roadblocks with burning vehicles across the municipality.
articles.description: Flores climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán-Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation

articles.headline: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar promises support for Toyota vehicle manufacturing expansion
articles.title: Karnataka CM’s Japan visit: D.K. Shivakumar promises support for Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing expansion plans in State
articles.summary: During a meeting at the Motomachi plant in Japan on November 23, 2026, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Industries Minister M.B. Patil assured Toyota Motor Corporation of state support to scale vehicle production to one million. Led by CEO Masakazu Yoshimura, the automaker discussed hybrid and flex-fuel technologies, while officials invited leadership to the upcoming Global Investors Meet.
articles.description: Toyota looks at scaling its vehicle production capacity to one million in the near future; D.K. Shivakumar and M.B. Patil invite company leadership to Global Investors’ Meet in Karnataka in 2027

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses PIL seeking municipal electoral roll corrections in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Supreme Court says, right to seek correction of electoral roll entry is personal, can't be pursued in PIL
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, dismissed a public interest litigation regarding house number discrepancies in municipal electoral rolls across Uttar Pradesh. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant and including Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ruled that correcting voter entries is a personal matter that individual voters must pursue through competent election authorities.
articles.description: A Bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it was not inclined to entertain the plea

articles.headline: Uttar Pradesh chief minister hails new direct rail link with Nepal
articles.title: Adityanath hails Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link as new chapter in India-Nepal cultural ties
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated on November 23, 2026, that a new direct rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur will strengthen spiritual ties between India and Nepal. The Saryu-Kamala Express, operating weekly via the 604-kilometre route starting November 28, is intended to facilitate pilgrimage for devotees and boost regional tourism according to official statements.
articles.description: ‘The centuries-old, unbroken emotional and cultural relationship between India and Nepal will now be further strengthened through modern rail connectivity,’ Yogi Adityanath said

articles.headline: Tata Steel announces strategic acquisition and partnership agreements with APL Apollo
articles.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo; another 26% via open offer
articles.summary: Tata Steel executed agreements to acquire a twenty six point six percent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for fifteen thousand five hundred ten crore rupees and announced a subsequent open offer for an additional twenty six percent stake. The strategic move aims to expand downstream operations in steel tubes and colour coated products, targeting enhanced production capacity and market growth alongside SG Tech Engineering Private Limited.
articles.description: Tata Steel to consolidate pipes and colour steel business under APL Apollo Tubes, buys entire promoter stake for ₹15,511 crore, to make ₹16,756 crore open offer

articles.headline: United Nations diplomats agree to discuss autonomous weapons rules over two years
articles.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
articles.summary: Diplomats meeting in Geneva failed to establish binding regulations for autonomous weapons during discussions. According to NPR, the United States, Russia, and Israel obstructed the proceedings. Representatives ultimately agreed to spend two years considering optional guidelines instead of the urgent legally binding framework requested by the International Committee of the Red Cross.
articles.description: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called "killer robots." Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to "start discussing options" after a largely fruitless week of negotiations. According to NPR: Before the negotiations got underway, the […]

articles.headline: PM Modi meets Nepal PM Balendra Shah, both exchange gifts including Gangajal and Rudraksha in Delhi
articles.title: PM Modi meets Nepal PM Balendra Shah, both exchange gifts including Gangajal and Rudraksha in Delhi
articles.description: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House on Monday and exchanged gifts during his maiden state visit to India since taking office in March. PM Modi gifted a Gangajal to Shah & recieved a Rudraksha in return.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs petitioner to move Allahabad High Court over Saharanpur mosque demolition
articles.title: Supreme Court asks petitioner to move Allahabad High Court over ‘demolition’ of 100-year-old mosque at Saharanpur
articles.summary: On November 23, 2026, the Supreme Court declined to directly hear a contempt plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal regarding the demolition of a century-old mosque in Saharanpur. The Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant instructed the petitioner to approach the Allahabad High Court to establish facts concerning alleged violations of demolition guidelines.
articles.description: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court

articles.headline: Viral video of earthmover at Sheshnag lake sparks outrage among parties and locals
articles.title: Earthmover at Amarnath Yatra stopover Sheshnag lake draws outrage from parties and locals
articles.summary: A viral video showing heavy machinery operating near the high-altitude Sheshnag lake in south Kashmir's Pahalgam drew widespread condemnation on November 23, 2026. Political figures including Peoples Democratic Party spokesman Mohit Bhan and cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq criticized the activity, warning that construction in the fragile glacial zone endangers the alpine ecosystem and downstream communities.
articles.description: Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region

articles.headline: Taliban deploys police to protect Afghanistan’s vanishing forests
articles.title: Taliban deploys police to protect Afghanistan’s vanishing forests
articles.description: Afghanistan’s last remaining forests are being guarded by a Taliban-run police force known as Green Units.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi's Gaza remarks trigger backlash from Left parties
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Gaza remarks expose old fault lines between Congress and Left
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi's remarks during a University of Chicago interaction linking the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel to Palestinian deaths sparked sharp criticism from Left parties. The disagreement exposed ideological differences between the Congress party and the Left within the INDIA bloc, echoing previous tensions from 2008 when the Left withdrew support from the UPA government.
articles.description: The backlash from Left parties to the Congress leader’s comments on Israel and Gaza underscores enduring ideological differences within the Opposition alliance

articles.headline: Kerala researchers link skin fairness creams to nephrotic syndrome cases
articles.title: In search of skin lightening creams, kidneys take a hit
articles.summary: Researchers from Kerala have published a study describing 15 cases of membranous nephropathy linked to the regular use of skin fairness creams. Doctors at Aster MIMS Hospital in Malappuram district found high levels of mercury in patients and products, with some creams exceeding permissible limits by 10,000 times, causing severe kidney injury and proteinuria.
articles.description: Researchers from Kerala have reported a series of cases from Malappuram district where the regular use of fairness creams has been linked to nephrotic syndrome. Heavy metal screening of the blood and urine samples of these patients revealed high levels of mercury, the toxic effects of which are well-known

articles.headline: Doctors warn against hazardous fairness creams after teenager develops kidney ailment
articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.summary: Medical professionals in Keralam's Malappuram district revealed on Friday that a 17-year-old girl was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy after using an online fairness cream containing mercury. Experts attribute the incident to unregulated online beauty products promoted by social media influencers. Consequently, the Keralam Drugs Control department launched student awareness campaigns and market inspections to prevent further heavy metal poisoning cases.
articles.description: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

articles.headline: Chief Justice Surya Kant recuses himself from Supertech insolvency case
articles.title: CJI Surya Kant recuses himself from hearing plea related to Supertech projects
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant recused himself from a plea concerning Supertech insolvency and homebuyers on Monday, November 23, 2026, after noting that one applicant was personally known to him. The bench had previously reserved its order on November 16 regarding state-owned National Buildings Construction Corporation completing sixteen stalled housing projects for debt-ridden Supertech Limited.
articles.description: "One of the applicants was incidentally known to me. I will have to constitute a special bench... He is remotely known to me, not my client or my relative, but known to me. Somebody should have been conscious of this fact. Why unnecessarily become a party? says CJI

articles.headline: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to visit Russia for bilateral talks
articles.title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to undertake official visit to Russia
articles.summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will embark on his first official visit to Russia starting November 30 to discuss energy cooperation, trade, and investment agreements. According to Dawn, the three day trip will feature talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin regarding industrial revival and oil sectors. Following Russia, the Prime Minister will travel to Iran for the Economic Cooperation Organisation Summit.
articles.description: The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements

articles.headline: Pratham NGO supports women school dropouts preparing for board exams
articles.title: In 12 states, NGO Pratham’s Second Chance Programme is helping women school dropouts appear for their Class X Board exams
articles.summary: Pratham Education Foundation operates its Second Chance Programme across 12 Indian states to help women and girls who left education early prepare for Class X board examinations. The initiative tackles unique regional hurdles through community mobilisation and flexible classes. According to data from the Ministry of Education, approximately 24 lakh students fail Class X annually across the country.
articles.description: As a significant percentage of older girls and women in India have not completed secondary education, this 14-year-old initiative focuses on helping them restart their educational journey and direct it towards earning a livelihood

articles.headline: Indian Oil Corporation prepares for domestic sustainable aviation fuel commercialisation
articles.title: India readies to take off on SAF, as CORSIA deadline approaches
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corporation has secured certification for sustainable aviation fuel production ahead of the upcoming Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation phase in January 2027. This initiative marks a crucial step in establishing domestic fuel alternatives and addressing carbon emissions directly at the source for international carriers operating out of India, according to the recent announcement.
articles.description: Mandatory second phase of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation becomes effective from January 2027, bringing a wider group of international airlines, including Indian carriers, under binding carbon-offsetting obligations

articles.headline: India defeats Sri Lanka by 317 runs to achieve series sweep
articles.title: Ind vs SL, third ODI | Kohli, Gill power India to series sweep with record 317-run win
articles.summary: India secured a record 317-run victory over Sri Lanka at the Greenfield Stadium, completing a three-nil series sweep. Centuries from Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli helped push the total to 390 for five before Mohammed Siraj took four wickets to dismiss the visiting team for just 73 runs in 22 overs, breaking previous historical margin records.
articles.description: Virat Kohli scored a quickfire 166, while Gill scored 116 that propelled India to a massive score

articles.headline: Veteran Malayalam cinema actor Innocent passes away at age 75
articles.title: Veteran actor and former MP Innocent passes away
articles.summary: Innocent, a renowned comedic actor and former parliamentarian, passed away in a Kochi hospital at the age of 75 following respiratory ailments and multi-organ failure. He acted in approximately 500 Malayalam films, served as president of the Association of Malayalam Movie Artists, and made political history by winning the Chalakudy Lok Sabha seat in 2014.
articles.description: A cancer survivor, he had been keeping unwell for a while and was undergoing treatment at a private hospital. The funeral will be held at St Thomas Cathedral at 10 a.m. on March 28.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate summons political figures and officials in Moga land probe
articles.title: ED summons AAP MLA, family members in probe against Moga legislator Amandeep Kaur Arora
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has issued summons to a Dharamkot member of the legislative assembly, local government officials, and family members of Moga legislator Amandeep Kaur Arora in connection with a money laundering investigation. The federal probe centers on alleged manipulation of revenue records that resulted in wrongful compensation disbursements for land acquired for highway construction.
articles.description: After searches were conducted against Ms. Kaur Arora earlier this month, the ED issued a statement and alleged that she and her husband facilitated the siphoning of compensation funds the government gave to locals in Moga district whose land was acquired for constructing a highway

articles.headline: Cricket fans urge removal of politics from India and Pakistan matches
articles.title: India-Pakistan cricket fans want ‘dirty politics’ kept out of beloved sport
articles.summary: Spectators at the Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha expressed frustration over the increasing politicisation of cricket rivalries between India and Pakistan. While players engaged in on-field friction, fans in the stands mingled peacefully and called on cricket boards to take disciplinary action against aggressive behavior that they believe is driven by politicians.
articles.description: Cricket's die-hard fans say players are being forced to take part in acts of aggression for the benefit of politicians.

articles.headline: Pakistan prime minister postpones Russia visit amid border and domestic tensions
articles.title: Pakistan PM cancels trip to Russia over regional clashes
articles.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called off his scheduled diplomatic journey following escalating cross-border military engagements with Afghanistan and widespread domestic demonstrations triggered by the death of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Officials confirmed the postponement on March 1, 2026, noting that new travel dates will be determined later through mutual discussions between Islamabad and Moscow.
articles.description: “In view of the current regional and internal situation, the Prime Minister has decided to postpone his visit to Russia after consultations,” Mr. Sharif’s office said

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir Police arrest twenty individuals in recruitment examination cheating case
articles.title: How J&K recruitment Board’s cheating case put a spotlight on Lok Bhavan, CM office powers? | Explained
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police arrested twenty individuals following allegations of unfair means during the Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment examination conducted by the J and K Service Selection Board. Officers seized electronic devices and uncovered modules operating across examination centres. The incident intensified political debate surrounding Union Territory governance powers and prompted student protests demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation probe.
articles.description: The incident has once again put a spotlight on the powers delineated between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in J&K as a Union Territory (UT), as the elected government claimed the Board was being run by the J&K Lieutenant Governor and not Chief Minister Omar Abdullah

articles.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot delegations conclude latest coalition talks without final agreement
articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
articles.summary: Representatives for caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political rival Gadi Eisenkot met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya on November 22, 2026. The discussions concluded without establishing a coalition government, though both parties confirmed follow-up meetings would occur. Eisenkot faces a December 6 deadline to form a government after recent elections failed to yield an absolute majority.
articles.description: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

articles.headline: Gujarat government prohibits display of caste signage on all private vehicles
articles.title: Gujarat Government amends law, prohibits display of caste-identifying signage on private vehicles
articles.summary: The Gujarat government notified the Gujarat Motor Vehicles Third Amendment Rules 2026, explicitly prohibiting caste identifying words symbols signs or text on private vehicles. Officials stated that the amendment to Rule 138 brings caste based displays under strict regulatory control. Draft rules were previously published on June 11, 2026, and final regulations were implemented after the stipulated objection period passed without feedback.
articles.description: Under this amendment, caste-identifying signs have now been explicitly included in the provisions governing advertising devices and figures displayed on vehicles

articles.headline: FBI national criminal database suffers suspected security breach
articles.title: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
articles.summary: United States media reports indicated that the National Crime Information Center experienced a compromise affecting law enforcement agencies nationwide. United States President Donald Trump commented on the situation during a media appearance, suggesting potential investigative insights might emerge from the incident. The development follows a series of recent cybersecurity disruptions impacting various federal departments, while agency leadership has faced ongoing scrutiny regarding internal security measures.
articles.description: The reported hacking is the latest in ​a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces severe coastal erosion along thirty-one percent of shorelines
articles.title: How ports and cyclones are eroding Andhra Pradesh’s coastline
articles.summary: Satellite mapping by the National Centre for Coastal Research under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences revealed that nearly thirty-one percent of Andhra Pradesh's coastline is eroding. Published in February 2024, the Shoreline Change Atlas indicated severe losses concentrated in delta districts like Kakinada and West Godavari, while local experts noted direct wave impacts along Visakhapatnam roads.
articles.description: Nearly 31% (318.96 km) of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline is eroding, with about 91.6 km falling into the ‘high erosion’ category. While the losses are concentrated in the delta districts of Kakinada, West Godavari, and Krishna, the coastal port district of Visakhapatnam is also facing the issue. Paul Nicodemus explores how decades of port development, changing wave patterns, and cyclones have contributed to the erosion of the City of Destiny’s beaches

articles.headline: Australia defeats Netherlands by 309 runs in World Cup match
articles.title: AUS vs NED | Maxwell puts on a big show, rips the Netherlands apart
articles.summary: Australia secured a massive 309-run victory against the Netherlands at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on October 25, 2023, setting a new tournament record for the largest margin of victory. Glenn Maxwell smashed the fastest World Cup century in 40 balls, finishing with 106 runs to propel Australia to a total of 399 for eight before bowler Adam Zampa claimed four wickets to dismiss the Netherlands for just 90 runs.
articles.description: Warner’s sixth hundred in the World Cup sets the tone for a massive total of 399 before the Aussies blow away the Men in Orange to secure a victory by a record margin; Zampa registers a third four-for on the trot

articles.headline: International Cricket Council introduces new playing conditions effective October 1
articles.title: Explained | When are the new ICC rules coming into play?
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council has implemented several updates to its playing conditions starting October 1, endorsed by both the Men's and Women's Cricket Committees led by former Indian captain Sourav Ganguly. Notably, the practice of running out a non-striking batter backing up too far, known as mankading, has been recategorized from unfair play to standard run outs following persistent debates across international fixtures.
articles.description: Will ‘mankading’ no longer be considered unfair? What about the use of saliva to polish a ball? What are some other key changes? Can hybrid pitches be used for all matches now?

articles.headline: Australia secures women's T20 series win against India
articles.title: India vs Australia Women’s T20 I Classy Perry sets up Australia’s series win
articles.summary: Australia clinched an unassailable 3-1 lead in the bilateral series after defeating India by seven runs in the fourth match at the Brabourne Stadium on December 18, 2022. Ellyse Perry remained unbeaten on 72 alongside Grace Harris as the visitors posted 188 for three, overcoming a late offensive from Indian batter Richa Ghosh to secure the victory ahead of the final fixture.
articles.description: A late assault by Richa Ghosh towards the end may have worried the Australians a bit, but India needed 20 off the last over and Meghan Schutt gave away only 12

articles.headline: Bisleri defends packaged drinking water safety after regulatory prosecution sanction
articles.title: Bisleri says it’s water ‘safe for consumption’ after FSSAI sanctions prosecution, says it has received no notice
articles.summary: Bisleri International has stated that its packaged drinking water remains safe for consumption, disputing Food Safety and Standards Authority of India findings that led to prosecution. The issue stems from a September 2025 sample at its Goa facility showing high bromate levels. Although a referral laboratory detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons, independent tests disputed the results, and Bisleri reported receiving no official notice.
articles.description: The company said five of six samples collected from its Goa facility in September 2025 met applicable standards, while an independent test found the bromate level in the disputed sample within the prescribed limit

articles.headline: Syria and EU negotiate normalisation deal amid European repatriation concerns
articles.title: As Syria-EU talks progress, diplomats fear focus will be on repatriation
articles.summary: Diplomats from Syria and the European Union are working to normalise relations and remove remaining sanctions after a 15-year suspension following the downfall of Bashar al-Assad's regime. European officials have expressed concerns that rising right-wing sentiment might cause Brussels to prioritise migrant repatriations over crucial human rights issues, even as both sides seek to build a framework for trade and political cooperation.
articles.description: Syria and the EU are in talks on trade and political ties, but migration will likely be the key issue for discussion.

articles.headline: Sri Lanka defeats Netherlands by five wickets in World Cup chase
articles.title: NED vs SL | Samarawickrama guides Islanders home for their first victory
articles.summary: Sri Lanka achieved its first victory of the tournament by successfully chasing a target of 262 against the Netherlands with five wickets and 10 balls remaining at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Stadium on October 21, 2023. Sadeera Samarawickrama led the successful run chase with an unbeaten 91 runs after lower-order batters Sybrand Engelbrecht and Logan van Beek established a record 130-run partnership for the Netherlands.
articles.description: A perfectly paced chase gave the former champion its first win in the World Cup.

articles.headline: Ollie Pope hits unbeaten century to give England hope in first Test
articles.title: Ind vs Eng 1st Test | Pope’s unbeaten hundred gives England hope on dramatic day
articles.summary: Ollie Pope recorded an unbeaten 148 runs at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium on January 27, 2024, helping England establish a 126-run lead over India on the third day of the first Test match. After India claimed a 190-run first-innings lead, Pope partnered with Ben Foakes for 112 runs to rescue the visiting side from a precarious position caused by Indian bowlers and spinner Joe Root.
articles.description: His unbeaten 148 helps Stokes’ men end the third day 126 ahead with four wickets in hand; he shares a crucial century stand with Foakes after Bumrah and the spin twins have the visitors reeling at 163 for five in the second innings

articles.headline: New Zealand draws first Test against India after resilient batting display
articles.title: New Zealand’s Mitchell, Phillips frustrate India as first Test ends in draw
articles.summary: New Zealand secured a draw against India in the first Test match at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Monday, falling five wickets short of a victory target. Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips frustrated Indian bowlers with a crucial sixth-wicket partnership that consumed valuable time. The result drops New Zealand out of the top two positions in the 2025 to 2027 World Test Championship standings.
articles.description: New Zealand rescued a draw on the final day, surviving 120 overs in a fighting display to finish on 239-5 at the close.

articles.headline: Israeli strike hits food aid vehicle in Gaza, killing three
articles.title: Israeli strike hits food aid vehicle in Gaza, killing three
articles.description: Three Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air attack on a vehicle carrying food.

articles.headline: Iran expresses desire for diplomatic resolution to ongoing conflict
articles.title: Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms
articles.summary: Tehran officials stated a continued commitment to pursuing negotiated agreements following recent military hostilities involving the United States and Israel. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi emphasized the need for substantial guarantees from Washington during ongoing discussions facilitated by regional mediators. Meanwhile, United States President Donald Trump asserted that existing proposals from Tehran failed to meet American standards, as diplomatic and military tensions persist across the region.
articles.description: Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside Iran, he says, adding that ‘a fair solution’ could be reached; U.S. denies Iran fired at an F-16

articles.headline: Alberto Nunez Feijoo balances moderate appeal and hardline tactics ahead of elections
articles.title: Who is Alberto Feijoo, the conservative seeking to become Spain’s new PM?
articles.summary: Popular Party leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo faces a critical balancing act ahead of the November 29 elections in Spain. Opinion polls place his conservative party ahead of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's Socialists, though an absolute majority may require support from the far-right Vox party. Feijoo's campaign combines his administrative background with hardened stances on immigration and corruption to prevent voters from shifting toward Vox.
articles.description: The former career civil servant hopes to lead his Popular Party to victory in November 29 elections.

articles.headline: Eugene Torre reflects on his journey as Asia's first chess grandmaster
articles.title: Meet Eugene Torre, the pioneering Asian GM who beat Karpov and befriended Fischer
articles.summary: Eugene Torre, who achieved the title of Asia's first chess grandmaster in 1974, discusses the evolution of the sport in the continent and his historic career. According to an interview published by The Hindu on April 26, 2025, Torre also represented the Philippines in 23 Olympiads and assisted Bobby Fischer. He expresses joy over China and India reaching the top in modern chess.
articles.description: A trailblazer for chess in the continent, Torre changed perceptions by proving he could compete against the world’s best in the 70s and 80s.

articles.headline: Indian parents invest heavily in children's sports careers beyond cricket
articles.title: Is India becoming a sporting nation?
articles.summary: Families across India are increasingly supporting their children's athletic ambitions in disciplines like chess, shooting, and tennis by funding expensive training and travel. Published on September 2, 2022, by The Hindu, the report highlights young athletes such as Vaishnavi Girish Ramdas and Divya Deshmukh, noting that this shift is driven by homegrown sporting stars who have achieved international success over the past two decades.
articles.description: It may take a few decades to get there, but the signs are positive — with an increased interest in sports, young athletes, better support and facilities, and parents who are willing to go the extra mile

articles.headline: Antoaneta Stefanova discusses chess career and Bulgarian team success
articles.title: Antoaneta Stefanova — the World champion who was her country’s Prime Ministerial candidate
articles.summary: Antoaneta Stefanova, the former women's world chess champion and former Bulgarian prime ministerial candidate, talks about leading Bulgaria to success at recent international events despite federation suspensions. In an interview published by The Hindu on October 9, 2024, Stefanova praises India's dominance in chess and highlights the crucial role of parental support for young players, drawing from her experience as a former coach of R. Vaishali.
articles.description: Antoaneta Stefanova played on the top board for Bulgaria at the recent Chess Olympiad and led Bulgaria to the 10th position, two slots above the team’s seeding

articles.headline: Nine people shot during a concert in central California town
articles.title: Central California concert shooting: Nine people shot; one in critical condition
articles.summary: Nine individuals were wounded during a concert in Strathmore, California, with one victim remaining in critical condition following surgery for a chest injury. The Tulare County Sheriff's Department stated that approximately 150 people attended the event. Authorities reported no immediate threat to the public and suggested the incident may be gang-related, though no arrests have yet been announced.
articles.description: Authorities said that they believe the shooting ‘may be gang-related’ but didn’t elaborate

articles.headline: Yemeni Houthis launch ballistic missiles toward Riyadh following coalition operation
articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.summary: Armed factions based in Yemen executed retaliatory aerial attacks targeting the Saudi Arabian capital following a military operation conducted by a coalition supporting the recognized government. Coalition representatives reported intercepting multiple incoming projectiles, although structural damage occurred near the border region. The cross-border escalations follow months of renewed fighting in the civil conflict, raising international concern regarding regional stability and civilian safety.
articles.description: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20

articles.headline: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
articles.summary: An Israeli military attack killed three Palestinians inside a vehicle carrying food and papers for the World Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on November 21, 2026. Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses confirmed the strike, while the charity stated the vehicle was unaffiliated. The Israeli military reported targeting militants in the area without explaining the vehicle strike. The incident occurred amid ongoing violence following an October 2025 United States-backed ceasefire.
articles.description: Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack

articles.headline: Cargo ship struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad hit by drones, Finland tightens security
articles.summary: A cargo ship traveling to Russia's Kaliningrad exclave was struck by drones in international waters within the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026, according to Russian and Finnish authorities. The vessel caught fire and drifted into Finnish territorial waters. Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko reported two drone strikes near Gogland island. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo warned that the war was spreading to neighboring regions as local security measures were tightened.
articles.description: Finland's Defence Ministry said the military had reintroduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution to protect civilians and enable authorities ​to operate if drones needed ‌to be intercepted.

articles.headline: Parliament sets longest unprorogued period record following Monsoon Session adjournment
articles.title: What does the Constitution say about proroguing Parliament? | Explained
articles.summary: Parliament concluded its Monsoon Session with an adjournment sine die on August 13. Officials confirmed the legislature has not yet been prorogued, establishing the longest unprorogued duration on record. Under Article 85 of the Constitution, the President summons Parliament upon ministerial advice, requiring sessions at least twice annually with gaps not exceeding six months.
articles.description: Why has Parliament not been prorogued after adjournment sine die? Can the Houses reconvene without it?

articles.headline: Indian stock markets decline in early trade amid global sell-off
articles.title: Stock markets decline in early trade amid global sell-off, profit taking after two-day rally
articles.summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty drifted lower in early trade on November 23, 2026, driven by a sharp global sell-off and profit taking following a two-day rally. The BSE Sensex declined 243.95 points to 83,675.76, while the NSE Nifty dropped 110.10 points to 25,672. Major laggards included Tata Steel and Axis Bank, according to market data.
articles.description: From the Sensex pack, Tata Steel, Axis Bank, UltraTech Cement, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and InterGlobe Aviation were among the major laggards

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills two in Kryvyi Rih
articles.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills 2
articles.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, killed two people and wounded sixty others on November 21, 2026. City administration head Oleksandr Vilkul reported that subsequent rockets struck emergency crews responding to the initial explosions. The assault damaged numerous residential buildings, a hospital, schools, and vehicles. The escalation coincided with increased tensions surrounding international mediation efforts and separate military incidents involving Poland and a Russian cargo ship.
articles.description: The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington; It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland

articles.headline: Delhi court frames charges against fourteen in NEET paper leak
articles.title: NEET paper leak case: Delhi court frames charges against 14 accused
articles.summary: A Delhi court formally framed charges against fourteen individuals on November 21, 2026, regarding the NEET-UG paper leak case, initiating trial proceedings for November 25, 2026. Special Judge Ajay Gupta instituted the charges after the accused pleaded not guilty to offences including cheating and criminal breach of trust. Public servants engaged by the National Testing Agency and eleven private individuals face prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Prevention of Corruption Act.
articles.description: Special Judge Ajay Gupta framed the charges after noting the accused pleaded ‘not guilty’, with the trial set to begin on a day-to-day basis from November 25

articles.headline: Congress criticises SEBI proposals to review foreign portfolio investor rules
articles.title: Congress attacks government over SEBI’s proposal to remove disclosure norms for FPIs
articles.summary: The opposition Congress party criticised market regulator SEBI for proposing a review of disclosure frameworks for foreign portfolio investors. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that the proposed changes would reintroduce opaque offshore ownership structures into Indian financial markets. The Securities and Exchange Board of India defended the consultation paper by stating the changes aim to align regulations with global standards.
articles.description: Ease of doing business cannot come at the cost of capital market integrity, says Jairam Ramesh

articles.headline: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sanctions Bisleri prosecution
articles.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample failed regulatory standards for bromate limits and polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. A referral laboratory confirmed the findings under the Food Safety and Standards Act. Additionally, the regulator suspended licences for other firms, ordered product recalls, and increased enforcement actions against food operators this year.
articles.description: "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said

articles.headline: Pakistan minister visits Delhi for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation dialogue
articles.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue ‘leaves options open’ for Pakistan SCO meets next year, say sources

articles.description: Army plans to invoke emergency powers to detonate 4 tonnes of lead azide in an Iowa town, despite a court-ordered stay.

articles.headline: Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari dies in Rome at age 89
